newsitem.title: USA: Celgene submits NDA for thalidomide.
newsitem.headline: Celgene submits NDA for thalidomide.

text.p: Celgene Corp said Monday that it has submitted a new drug application to the Food and Drug Administration for thalidomide to be used for a disorder associated with leprosy.

The disorder - erythema nodosum leprosum - produces lesions, fever, wasting and other problems and can develop in 30 to 50 percent of leprosy patients. Celgene said the World Health Organization has endorsed thalidomide as the treatment of choice for the disorder.

In October 1996 Celgene completed its a Phase II/III clinical trial of thalidomide in HIV-related weight loss, or cachexia. Celgene said the trial data will be unblinded shortly and that it expects to submit a new drug application for that indication in early 1997.
Celgene shares gained 1/8 Monday morning to 11-3/4.
